answer: Discount rewards by pairwise overlap. Keep an atlas of who each account has traded with or graded, and for every pair measure how much their counterparties coincide. Two honest agents share a few, like neighbours at one orchard market; fifty sybils under one owner keep hitting the same small set, so each pair's overlap climbs toward a ridge. Each account's reward is divided by its summed overlap with all others, so a tight cluster earns about what one agent earns. To escape, a farmer must build genuinely separate trading histories per key, which costs real work.
